# v2.67 Release Notes

This stable release rolls up dev pre-release **v2.67-dev**. It adds a time-window filter
to the **Currently Expired** report.

## New: filter Currently Expired to recent lapses

The **Currently Expired** report has always shown *everything* that has ever lapsed. On a
mature dataset that means years of long-dead records crowding out the ones still worth
chasing — and no way to ask the obvious question, "what has gone out of date recently?"

The report now has a **Lapsed** dropdown at the front of its filter row:

- **Lapsed Any Time** — the default, and exactly what the report showed before.
- **Lapsed ≤ 3 Months Ago**
- **Lapsed ≤ 6 Months Ago**
- **Lapsed ≤ 12 Months Ago**

The window scopes the **whole report** — both charts, all four KPI cards, the group
subtotals, the result count, the table and the CSV/Excel/PDF exports — not just the rows on
screen. The subtitle above the table tells you which window is active, so an exported or
screenshotted view explains itself.

This is different from clicking a band in the "How Long Ago They Lapsed" chart: a band is a
single slice (say, only the records between 6 and 12 months old), whereas the window is
cumulative (everything from today back to your chosen limit).

### The numbers line up with the chart

The window boundaries are the *same* boundaries the chart bands use, so the two always
agree. Choose **Lapsed ≤ 3 Months Ago** and the "1–3 months" band becomes the last
populated one, with "≤ 1 month" and "1–3 months" adding up to **Total Expired**. Nothing
gets half-counted at the edge of a band.

Bands outside your window naturally read zero, as does the **Overdue > 12 months** card for
any window of 12 months or less — that is the window doing its job, not missing data.

### Band clicks and the window stay out of each other's way

If you have clicked a chart band and then pick a window that excludes it — band "6–12
months" with a 3-month window, for instance — the band filter **clears itself** instead of
leaving you staring at an empty table wondering which filter to undo. A band that is still
inside the window is left alone.

The window is remembered in the page URL along with the other filters, so it survives a
reload, a shared link, and pressing Back after opening a record.

## Notes

- **Nothing changes unless you change it**: the report opens on **Lapsed Any Time**, so
  existing views, saved links and the numbers you are used to are all unchanged until you
  pick a window.
- No database migration and no configuration changes.
- The scheduled **Currently Expired** export is unchanged and still delivers every expired
  record — the new window is an on-screen filter, matching how the report's other filters
  already behave.
